text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Safe prescribing of controlled drugs: a brown-bag reconciliation of every medicine, a prescription drug monitoring program check before every controlled prescription, a written single-prescriber agreement with one pharmacy, urine drug testing explained as part of care, seven-day supplies at first, a locked box, and take-back of unused tablets; no controlled drug stopped abruptly
  • Addiction medicine consultation to make the substance use diagnoses, start medication for opioid use disorder, and plan the benzodiazepine change and taper
  • Overdose prevention: naloxone nasal spray at home and in the tour bag, two people around him taught to use it, no alcohol or other sedatives, and the danger of opioids with benzodiazepines and with the sleep apnea that is suspected explained
  • Safety: a structured safety assessment, a written safety plan, firearms locked and unloaded with ammunition separate, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit; PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at each review
  • Buprenorphine for opioid use disorder: buprenorphine with naloxone started in the office at a COWS score above 8, 16 mg a day, weekly contact for the first month, prescriptions from this clinic only, counseling, and no tapering off while he is doing well; buprenorphine is not withheld because he takes a benzodiazepine
  • Benzodiazepine change and taper: alprazolam combined into diazepam (40 mg a day), held steady until buprenorphine is stable, then reduced by about 5 to 10% every two to four weeks, paused during engagements, illness or withdrawal symptoms, never stopped abruptly; CBT for anxiety and insomnia alongside; no Z-drug or other sedative in its place
  • Hypertension: home readings confirmed stage 2 hypertension, so two first-line drugs were started in one pill (amlodipine with valsartan), with potassium and creatinine two to four weeks later, a target below 130/80, sodium reduction, activity and weight loss
  • Obstructive sleep apnea: CPAP from the split-night titration, with adherence data reviewed at each visit and a travel machine for tours; no sedative added at night
  • Weight treated without stigma: earlier meals, protein and fiber, more walking and karate between tours, and tirzepatide once weekly, chosen because it also treats obstructive sleep apnea with obesity, raised slowly with a watch on nausea and constipation
  • Constipation on opioids: polyethylene glycol daily with senna as needed, fluids and fiber; a peripherally acting opioid antagonist only if these fail; an abdominal radiograph only for pain, distension or vomiting
  • Glaucoma: latanoprost continued, his ophthalmologist kept informed of every new medicine, no phentermine, decongestant or anticholinergic sleep aid, steroids only when essential and with his ophthalmologist's knowledge, and urgent care for eye pain with halos
  • Performing and touring: no medication change in the week before an engagement, weekly video visits while away, controlled prescriptions sent only to one named pharmacy, a written plan for missed doses, naloxone and any prescribed devices in the tour bag, and a letter he controls for venues

resource.title: Elvis Presley synthetic care plan
resource.description: Polypharmacy and prescription opioid and sedative use disorders from several prescribers, in a 39-year-old touring singer who comes in for fatigue, weight gain, constipation, sleepiness and high blood pressure. The episode covers a brown-bag medication reconciliation and prescription drug monitoring program review that finds two opioids, two benzodiazepines and an appetite suppressant from five prescribers; a nonjudgmental DSM-5-TR assessment; naloxone at the first visit; a single-prescriber agreement; buprenorphine started in the office under the ASAM 1968 guideline, with the guideline's advice that taking a benzodiazepine is not a reason to withhold it; the benzodiazepines combined into diazepam and tapered slowly under the 1973 joint guideline; a structured safety assessment with means safety and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; hypertension confirmed with home readings and treated under the 1973 AHA/ACC guideline; obesity treated without stigma with tirzepatide, which also treats obstructive sleep apnea; STOP-Bang and in-laboratory polysomnography because opioids make home testing unreliable; opioid-induced constipation; glaucoma that rules out phentermine and anticholinergic sleep aids; acute back pain managed on buprenorphine; and care planned around a performing and touring schedule.

Buprenorphine for opioid use disorder: buprenorphine with naloxone started in the office at a COWS score above 8, 16 mg a day, weekly contact for the first month, prescriptions from this clinic only, counseling, and no tapering off while he is doing well; buprenorphine is not withheld because he takes a benzodiazepine

Benzodiazepine change and taper: alprazolam combined into diazepam (40 mg a day), held steady until buprenorphine is stable, then reduced by about 5 to 10% every two to four weeks, paused during engagements, illness or withdrawal symptoms, never stopped abruptly; CBT for anxiety and insomnia alongside; no Z-drug or other sedative in its place

Hypertension: home readings confirmed stage 2 hypertension, so two first-line drugs were started in one pill (amlodipine with valsartan), with potassium and creatinine two to four weeks later, a target below 130/80, sodium reduction, activity and weight loss
Obstructive sleep apnea: CPAP from the split-night titration, with adherence data reviewed at each visit and a travel machine for tours; no sedative added at night

Weight treated without stigma: earlier meals, protein and fiber, more walking and karate between tours, and tirzepatide once weekly, chosen because it also treats obstructive sleep apnea with obesity, raised slowly with a watch on nausea and constipation

Constipation on opioids: polyethylene glycol daily with senna as needed, fluids and fiber; a peripherally acting opioid antagonist only if these fail; an abdominal radiograph only for pain, distension or vomiting

Glaucoma: latanoprost continued, his ophthalmologist kept informed of every new medicine, no phentermine, decongestant or anticholinergic sleep aid, steroids only when essential and with his ophthalmologist's knowledge, and urgent care for eye pain with halos

Performing and touring: no medication change in the week before an engagement, weekly video visits while away, controlled prescriptions sent only to one named pharmacy, a written plan for missed doses, naloxone and any prescribed devices in the tour bag, and a letter he controls for venues

note.text: Addiction medicine consultation to make the substance use diagnoses, start medication for opioid use disorder, and plan the benzodiazepine change and taper
